title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is axiomatizing his 1986 'analysis situs' structures. The previous page contrasts two equivalent presentations. The 'magasin' presentation is a poset M with relations ≪, |o| and a family F ⊂ P(M). The 'atlas' presentation is a poset F of figures with relations ≤, ≪, |o| and axioms At1–At5. This page introduces a third, 'symmetric' presentation that keeps both base sets and links them.

Data:
(a) an incidence relation X ◁ F between M (elements Grothendieck calls multistates, or possibly 'multistrates') and F (figures), which is meant to induce ≤ on both sets;
(b) relations ≪ and |o| on M.

For F ∈ F put F̃ = {X ∈ M | X ◁ F}, and define F ≤ G iff F̃ ⊂ G̃.

Axioms:
- AtM1 (separation on both sides, as in a reduced formal context or extensional Chu space).
  - a) F ↦ F̃, F → P(M) is injective, so ≤ on F is an order.
  - b) The family F̃ separates the points of M (a T0-type condition).
- AtM2 ('quasi-admissible'). For each X, F^X = {F | X ◁ F} has a least element F_X, the elementary figure of X. Hence X ◁ F ⇔ F_X ≤ F ⇔ X ∈ F̃. Given AtM1 a), AtM1 b) is equivalent to X ↦ F_X, M → F being injective.
- AtM3.
  - a) F̃ is closed under unions of families bounded above by a member of F̃ (bounded completeness).
  - b) F ≠ ∅, equivalently ∅ ∈ F̃ (by AtM3 a with the empty family), equivalently F̃ has a least element. The margin notes this is automatic when M ≠ ∅, by AtM2.

Next page: M gets the order X ≤ Y ⇔ F_X ≤ F_Y, with X̃ = M_{≤X}. Each F̃ is a down-set, and down-closed subsets of members of F̃ are again in F̃. Compatibility F ⋎ G ('sup exists') is required to be determined pointwise by compatibility of elements (AtM4), and is tied to |o| (AtM5).

In modern terms: F is the poset of down-closed, consistent subsets ('configurations') of the poset M. M sits inside F as the completely prime / join-irreducible elements F_X. This is the familiar duality between a prime-generated, bounded-complete poset and its poset of primes with a binary compatibility relation.

Purpose: show that the magasin, atlas and symmetric viewpoints give equivalent categories (groupoids), so the theory can be stated in whichever form is most convenient.
errors: No substantive mathematical error. The chain 'F ≠ ∅ ⇔ ∅ ∈ F̃ ⇔ F̃ ≠ ∅ ⇔ F̃ has a least element' silently uses AtM3 a) applied to the empty family; that is legitimate but should be said.

AtM1 and AtM2 are partly redundant in the final form, as Grothendieck himself notes: AtM1 b) becomes injectivity of X ↦ F_X. Also, AtM3 a) is weakened on purpose relative to the down-closure proposition on the next page.
The struck-out first version of AtM2 mixed 'covers M' and 'separates points'. The final version cleanly separates these into AtM1 b) and AtM2.

ideas.what: Presenting a structure as two sets with an incidence relation, separated on both sides, with the ordering on each side induced by the incidence.
ideas.modern_name: Reduced formal context / extensional separated Chu space; Galois connection induced by a relation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (polarities, 1940); Wille (Formal Concept Analysis, 1982); Barr, Chu (Chu spaces, 1979)

ideas.what: Quasi-admissibility: each point X has a least figure containing it, F_X. M embeds in F as the 'elementary figures', and incidence becomes F_X ≤ F.
ideas.modern_name: Principal down-sets / completely prime (join-irreducible) elements; object concepts
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard lattice/domain theory (Birkhoff; Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel 1981 for prime algebraic domains)

ideas.what: Closure of the figure family under bounded unions; the empty figure as the least element.
ideas.modern_name: Bounded completeness / consistently complete family of down-sets (configurations of an event structure)

ideas.what: Equivalence of three presentations ('magasin', 'atlas', 'symmetric') of the same analysis-situs structure, as equivalent groupoids.
ideas.modern_name: Duality between prime-algebraic, bounded-complete posets and posets with binary compatibility (prime event structures)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's magasin/atlas/symmetric equivalence, with the down-closure and pairwise-compatibility axioms (AtM2–AtM4 across this page and the next), is structurally the Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel duality between prime event structures and prime-algebraic coherent domains, found independently in a geometric (analysis situs) setting. The extra relations ≪ and |o| would then be extra geometric structure on an event structure. To my knowledge this link between his late combinatorial-topology axiomatics and concurrency/domain theory has not been noted.
missed.quote: AtM2 La famille de parties F̃ dans M est quasi-admissible, i.e. ∀X ∈ M, ... F^X a un plus petit élément (appelé la figure élémentaire associée à la multistate X)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could let historians and directed-topology or concurrency researchers read Grothendieck's 1986 analysis situs drafts as a domain/event-structure theory with geometric extras. It might suggest an interpretation of ≪ and |o| (interiority, disjointness) as geometric enrichments of configuration structures.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but routine order-theoretic axiomatization: an incidence structure separated on both sides, least elements, and bounded unions. Its content is standard in lattice and domain theory. Interest lies only in its role in Grothendieck's unpublished 1986 analysis-situs project and in the unremarked parallel with event-structure/domain duality.
transcription_corrections: Line under (a): '(remplissant[?] i définir ∈ sur M et sur F)' is more likely '(permettant de définir ≤ sur M et sur F)'; the symbol is ≤, not ∈.
'multistates' may actually read 'multistrates' (multi-strata), which would fit the stratified-space context of analysis situs. The handwriting is ambiguous and should be checked against other pages.
In the struck AtM2: 'on l'appelle la figuration[?] du multistate élémentaire défini par X' should probably read 'on l'appelle la figure élémentaire définie par X'.
In the definition of F̃ the bound variable should be X, not x: F̃ = {X ∈ M | X ◁ F}.
AtM3 a) parenthesis: '(stabilité de F̃ par ∪ majorées)' is plausible; read 'réunions majorées'.
Margin at AtM3 b): 'résulte des autres si M ≠ ∅' is confirmed.
